paul.name: Paul
paul.role: Letter speaker who hopes to visit the Roman believers
paul.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
paul.importance: He seeks encouragement from the believers as well as sharing his teaching.
paul.connections: His companions send greetings. Tertius names his own writing role.

jesus.name: Jesus Christ
jesus.role: The one through whom Paul describes God’s gift and welcome
jesus.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jesus.importance: His welcome supplies the pattern for receiving others across disputed practices.
jesus.connections: Paul connects his death and resurrection with the believers’ changed life.

word.languageNote: This is the dictionary form of the name “Christ.”

abraham.name: Abraham
abraham.role: Ancestor whose trust comes before circumcision
abraham.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abraham.importance: The order of promise and sign connects him with believers from different peoples.
abraham.connections: Sarah shares the promised birth despite their old age.

sarah.name: Sarah
sarah.role: Abraham’s wife whose condition makes the promised birth seem impossible
sarah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
sarah.importance: Her remembered condition makes the promise depend on God’s power rather than visible strength.
sarah.connections: Paul connects her body with Abraham’s old age and God’s promise.

david.name: David
david.role: Remembered king whose words Paul cites in his argument
david.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
david.importance: His cited words join earlier Scripture with the letter’s questions about mercy and failure.
david.connections: Paul names Jesus as David’s descendant and cites David’s words about forgiveness.

priscilla.name: Prisca, also called Priscilla
priscilla.role: Worker whom Paul greets with Aquila
priscilla.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
priscilla.importance: Their household and risk show the personal help behind Paul’s wider teaching task.
priscilla.connections: Paul says they risked their lives for him. A church meets in their house.

aquila.name: Aquila
aquila.role: Worker whom Paul greets with Prisca
aquila.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
aquila.importance: His shared work connects a household with the needs of a wider group of believers.
aquila.connections: A church meets in their house. Paul and Gentile churches thank them.

phoebe.name: Phoebe
phoebe.role: Servant or deacon of the church in Cenchreae
phoebe.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
phoebe.importance: Her previous help to many people supports Paul’s request for practical welcome.
phoebe.connections: Paul asks the Roman believers to welcome her and help with her needs.

tertius.name: Tertius
tertius.role: Writer who adds his own greeting within Paul’s letter
tertius.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
tertius.importance: His named writing role makes another person’s contribution visible within the letter.
tertius.connections: He greets the Roman believers alongside Paul’s other companions.

timothy.name: Timothy
timothy.role: Worker who sends greetings with Paul’s companions
timothy.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
timothy.importance: His greeting connects the letter’s readers with workers beyond Paul alone.
timothy.connections: Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater also send greetings in the same verse.
